events_chronological: As a boy in a working-class quarter, a teenager parks cars for the crew across the road and decides that being a gangster beats being head of state.
He is arrested for selling stolen cigarettes and comes out of court to find the whole crew waiting to congratulate him for saying nothing.
He and two older men hijack lorries out of the airport and move the loads on.
He meets the woman he will marry, and when a neighbour assaults her he pistol-whips the man on his own drive and hands her the gun to hide.
The two marry, and she learns to live with the money, the absences and the other men's wives.
The volatile one of the pair stabs and shoots a protected man in their own club, and the three of them drive the body upstate to bury it.
Six months later they have to dig the body up again because the land has been sold.
He installs a mistress in a flat, and his wife finds out and holds a revolver to his face while he sleeps.
He and the older man burn down a restaurant they have stripped through a paper credit line.
He is jailed for beating a gambler who complained to his sister, and runs food and drugs from inside the prison.
He is released and starts dealing heroin against the boss's express orders, pulling in his wife and both friends.
The crew take six million out of the airport cargo terminal in a single night.
The older man has nearly everyone involved killed as they begin spending the money where it can be seen.
The volatile one is told he is finally to be made and is shot through the head instead, in payment for the protected man.
In one frantic day he runs drugs, cooks a family dinner and is tailed by a helicopter, and is arrested that evening.
The boss gives him a few thousand and disowns him, and the older man tries to send him and his wife to a killing in the south.
He testifies against both of them and enters witness protection, ending up an ordinary man fetching his newspaper in a suburb.
nonlinear_category_reason: Fifteen of sixteen scenes run forward across thirty years; the exception is the killing in the car boot, played as a cold open and reached again a third of the way through.
syuzhet_notes: The telling opens with the three men stopping the car to finish off the man in the boot, then cuts to the narrator saying he always wanted to be a gangster and starts again thirty years earlier. It reaches that opening scene again at the eighth told bullet. Nothing else is out of order.
fabula_notes: The narration is retrospective throughout, but it is a voice over the action rather than a separate scene level, so the boot scene is a flash-forward rather than a frame.
